exact_title: SGLT-2 receptor inhibitors for treating patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
source_type: systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis

figures.title: Study selection flow diagram
figures.summary: 535 abstracts; 73 duplicates removed; 462 screened; 417 excluded; 45 full texts assessed; article states 13 trials included.

figures.title: Network plot—monotherapy (% achieving HbA1c <7%)
figures.summary: Placebo-centered network linking licensed SGLT-2 inhibitor doses; edge evidence is sparse for several agents.

figures.title: Network plot—dual therapy (% achieving HbA1c <7%)
figures.summary: Metformin-background network; fewer studies and sparse connections increase dependence on indirect evidence.

figures.title: Risk of bias
figures.summary: Most domains low risk; some unclear because reporting was inadequate; all included trials pharmaceutical-company funded.

figures.title: HbA1c <7%—monotherapy
figures.summary: All agents outperform placebo; canagliflozin 300 mg exceeds canagliflozin 100 mg and dapagliflozin 10 mg.

figures.title: Mean HbA1c change—monotherapy
figures.summary: Canagliflozin 300 mg has the largest reduction (1.23 percentage points vs placebo); several between-agent gaps are statistically credible.

figures.title: Mean weight change—monotherapy
figures.summary: Canagliflozin 100 mg shows greatest weight reduction; significant differences versus several other agents.

figures.title: Mean SBP change—monotherapy
figures.summary: All point estimates favor SGLT-2 inhibitors vs placebo; some intervals cross no effect; empagliflozin 10 mg differs from canagliflozin.

figures.title: HbA1c <7%—dual therapy
figures.summary: All assessed agents outperform placebo; empagliflozin doses and canagliflozin 300 mg rank toward the higher end.

figures.title: Mean HbA1c change—dual therapy
figures.summary: Canagliflozin 300 mg shows greatest base-case reduction (0.77 percentage points); between-agent differences are generally small.

figures.title: Mean weight change—dual therapy
figures.summary: Weight reductions range 1.63–2.5 kg vs placebo; canagliflozin 300 mg exceeds empagliflozin 10 mg.

figures.title: Mean SBP change—dual therapy
figures.summary: Base-case reductions favor all assessed agents versus placebo; no significant between-drug differences.

figures.title: Sensitivity: HbA1c <7%—dual therapy
figures.summary: Including Henry/Kashiwagi broadens the network and produces very wide ipragliflozin uncertainty.

figures.title: Sensitivity: weight—dual therapy
figures.summary: Canagliflozin 300 mg exceeds empagliflozin 10 mg and ipragliflozin 50 mg; other conclusions largely stable.

figures.title: Sensitivity: SBP—dual therapy
figures.summary: Including atypical trials materially changes rankings; dapagliflozin appears significantly better than all other flozins.

figures.title: Sensitivity: HbA1c—dual therapy
figures.summary: Bolinder inclusion worsens dapagliflozin relative ranking; ipragliflozin estimate is highly uncertain.

tables.title: Baseline characteristics of all included studies
tables.summary: Study-level design, setting, duration, baseline glycaemia, demographics, interventions, comparators and outcomes across the included RCTs.

tables.title: Summary data—monotherapy
tables.summary: Raw monotherapy baseline and outcome data feeding the networks; outcome availability varies by trial.

tables.title: Summary data—dual therapy
tables.summary: Raw metformin-background trial data feeding the dual-therapy networks; several outcomes are incompletely reported.

coverage_decision: All 16 main-text figures, all 3 main tables, the study-selection and Bayesian-analysis workflows, and the one-page search-strategy supplement were reconciled. References were excluded from atomization but extracted separately to Markdown.
omissions: Bibliography entries are provenance infrastructure and were not converted into LiteratureAtoms.
